newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta Drydocks cuts losses in first half.
newsitem.headline: Malta Drydocks cuts losses in first half.

text.p: State-owned Malta Drydocks cut losses in the first half of this year, the government said.

But the British consultants Appledore International said in an efficiency report made public by the government at the weekend that the yard was "fast approaching the point where it would be beyond redemption".

Prime Minister Alfred Sant told the Maltese Parliament on Friday that the yard lost 3.4 million Maltese pounds ($8.8 million) in the first six months of this year, just under two million pounds less than in the same period in 1996.

In February Sant stunned dockyard workers when he scrapped a council directly elected by workers to manage the yard and instead installed a council whose members were mostly appointed by the government.

He said the yard had been making losses for years, but the situation deteriorated sharply in 1995 and 1996 when losses totalled 25 million pounds ($65 million). Accumulated losses soared to over 70 million pounds ($182 million).

Appledore said Malta Drydocks had huge under-use of labour and should be split in two, one section employing 1,286 people and concentrating on ship repair and the other taking over the rest of the 3,200 workforce to concentrate on new business such as building buses for Malta.

"The situation at the dockyard is extremely serious ...however we believe that it has a future. We believe there is an opportunity to take advantage of three key factors -- location, low cost and technical competence," Appledore said.
The consultants said Malta Drydocks needed a better reputation among clients and government financial subsidies should be structured to send the right messages of success and best use of resources.
